title: Getting Started with R: An Interactive Guide
text:
This interactive guide will help you learn R from the ground up. You can run all code examples directly in your browser - just click the “Run Code” button in each code block!


The R console is where we interact with R. When you see a > symbol, that’s your prompt to enter commands. In the interactive code blocks below, you’ll be able to type and run R code directly.






Pro Tip



Don’t worry about making mistakes! Experimentation is a key part of learning. If you get an error, read the message carefully - R usually tells you what went wrong.

2. Variables and Assignment
Variables are like containers that store values. In R, we typically use the <- operator for assignment:














Naming Rules




Variable names can contain letters, numbers, dots (.) and underscores (_)
They must start with a letter or a dot
R is case-sensitive: Fish and fish are different variables
Use descriptive names: total_catch is better than tc

title: Visualizing Trends with ggplot2
text:
In this guide, we will learn how to visualize trends in data using ggplot2. We’ll use the cars dataset, which contains information on car speed and stopping distances.


A line plot is often used to visualize trends over time or any continuous variable. Although the cars dataset doesn’t have a time component, we can still visualize the trend of speed against stopping distance.











We can enhance the visualization by adding a smoothing line to better capture the underlying trend.











You can further customize trend lines by changing colors, line types, and smoothing methods. Let’s use a linear model (method = “lm”) to display the trend.











Finally, let’s compare different trend lines by plotting both a linear model and a loess smoother together.

title: R for Small-Scale Fishery Data
text:
This collection is designed to help you work with small-scale fishery data using R. The examples are tailored to practical use cases, leveraging ggplot2 and other tools to analyze and visualize fisheries data. All code can be run interactively in your browser using quarto-live, meaning no installation is necessary to start learning and applying these techniques.
These data science “snacks” are meant to provide you with hands-on experience for working with real-world fishery datasets. They can serve as quick, practical insights or as stepping stones to more advanced analysis in fisheries research.
